citations.title: Changing Profile of the Physical Therapy Professoriate—Are We Meeting CAPTE's Expectations?

citations.authors: Jette DU, Nelson L, Palaima M, Wetherbee E
citations.title: How do we improve quality in clinical education? Examination of structures, processes, and outcomes
citations.what_it_says: Analyzes DPT/tDPT curricular structures and finds limited integration of research training compared to PhD programs, indicating the tDPT is primarily a clinical credential rather than a pathway to independent investigator careers.

citations.authors: Jewell DV, Moore JD, Goldstein MS
citations.title: Delivering the physical therapy value proposition: a call to action
citations.what_it_says: Identifies that the clinical DPT/tDPT pipeline does not produce PhD-level scientists and calls for separate post-professional research training (PhD, postdoc) to build the profession's independent investigator workforce.

citations.authors: National Institutes of Health, Office of Extramural Research
citations.title: Physician-Scientist Workforce Working Group Report (updated implementation)
citations.what_it_says: NIH workforce analysis documents that K-award and R01 success among rehabilitation scientists is concentrated in PhD-trained investigators, with clinical doctorates such as the DPT/tDPT rarely appearing as terminal credentials of funded PIs.

citations.authors: Goldstein MS, Scalzitti DA, Craik RL, Dunn SL, Irion JM, Irrgang JJ, Kolobe THA, Tilson JK, Worthingham CA
citations.title: The revised research agenda for physical therapy
citations.what_it_says: APTA-endorsed research agenda explicitly distinguishes the tDPT (clinical credential) from the PhD/postdoctoral pathway required to develop independent, extramurally funded rehabilitation researchers.
